observability_triage.rationale: A level shifter is observable as a real powered logic component inserted in the schematic graph between the controller data output and LED DIN, with its high-side supply tied to the switched 5 V rail. LED supply connectivity can be checked independently from component prose.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A populated logic-level shifter/buffer component is electrically between the controller LED-data output and the first addressable LED DIN: the two endpoints are on different nets joined only through the shifter data path, the shifter high-side/logic supply is on switched 5V, and its ground and enable pins are validly connected.

setup: Build schematic and identify controller LED-data pin, first LED DIN, and candidate logic-buffer symbols.

parameters.trace: controller LED data to first LED DIN
parameters.required_component_class: level shifter or logic buffer rated for 5V output

expected_observations.subject: qualified level-shifter components on the data path
controller-side and LED-side data net names
direct controller-to-LED bypass paths excluding the shifter
unconnected mandatory ground or enable pins

determinism_controls: Classify the device from a frozen KiCad symbol/library allowlist and parsed pin roles.
Require actual pin/net connectivity and a matching populated PCB footprint.

setup: A component named level shifter exists but the controller data bypasses it.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The addressable LED power and logic high-side supply are connected to the switched 5 V rail generated by the power-board boost domain, not to 3V3.

setup: Resolve first LED supply pins and level-shifter high-side supply.

expected_observations.subject: resolved supply net for LED VDD and shifter high side

determinism_controls: Resolve explicit net connectivity and net-ties.
Do not infer supply from textual labels detached from pins.
